notes: TBox rule edit (verifier rebuild: the writer's boson rule was re-picked, because in its name world the photon stops being a boson, which with spin 1 makes it a fermion and contradicts firm facts outside the chain such as lasers and Bose-Einstein statistics of light, and its second member, the graviton, is hypothetical). Derivability very_unlikely: core hydrogen burning is what defines the main sequence (Wikipedia) and the rule is stated in general form; it follows from nothing more basic. No exceptions: a star that no longer fuses hydrogen in its core has left the main sequence by definition. Counterfactual: helium into carbon is what red giants do (plausible) and is clearly false for main-sequence stars. Determinate queries use invented stars named in the prompt (Kestrel-7, Orrin's Star). The indeterminate queries use the Sun, the one main-sequence star whose core fusion is stated by name ('the Sun fuses hydrogen into helium' 44, 'the Sun fuses hydrogen' 61); no other star's core fusion is stated by name often enough, so both queries turn on the same storage choice and there are two worlds (as with 'Is a tarantula a spider?'). Step 3: in w1 the Sun leaves the main sequence, a classification label; this contradicts no fact about anything outside the chain (it is a fact about the Sun, which goes with its fusion). In w2 the Sun burns helium, which contradicts only facts about the Sun itself (the stored fact giving way). Near query (the star closest to the Sun) does not depend on the rule and answers Proxima Centauri. Since 2026-10-31 (formal check, FINDINGS B3) the one-process presupposition is stated: 'a star's core does not fuse hydrogen into helium and helium into carbon at the same time' is a bridge of q2 and q3 (with a check) and a step of their chains; it is what makes the Sun's stored fusion clash with the edited rule, and what q1's original 'no' rests on (fuses_in_core stays untagged in RELATIONS.md).
